record.paper_title: Open problems about regular languages, 35 years later.
record.original_question: Given a regular language L over an alphabet A, define the star height of an extended regular expression to be the maximum nesting depth of the Kleene star operator when expressions are built from 0, 1, letters a in A, union, concatenation, complement, and star. Define the star height h(L) of L to be the minimum star height among all extended regular expressions representing L. Is there an algorithm that, for an arbitrary regular language L, computes h(L)?

evidence.quote:
The star height problem is the following question:
Problem 1. Is there an algorithm which computes the star height of a given regular language?

artifact.category_tag: generalized star height of regular languages
artifact.status_search_result: The generalized star-height problem — whether the star height of a regular language (with complement allowed in expressions) is computable — is a long-standing open problem in formal language theory. It is not even known whether every regular language has generalized star height at most 1. Partial results exist for restricted classes (e.g., languages recognized by Rees matrix semigroups over abelian groups have generalized star height ≤ 1), but no general algorithm is known.

status_evidence.title: Generalized star-height problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is an open question whether a nesting depth of more than 1 is required, and if so, whether there is an algorithm to determine the minimum required star height.
status_evidence.claim: The generalized star-height problem remains open.
